label: rare: re-fed "a" during copy (esp. short seqs with 3/c)
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.016% of steps). About 70% of activation mass is on copy-phase steps where the input is the letter a being fed back. It fires most strongly when a is the first original token, the sequence is short (L=3-4), and the next tokens to output are 3, c or v (top: a 3 3 <DEL> [a]). It fires on only ~0.8% of copy-phase a inputs, so precision is very low; no checked context condition raised precision above ~9% without losing most of the recall. The rest of the mass is in the original phase: a weak pattern at the token right after a 3 3 run (l, z, i, u), plus scattered other letters. It never fires at t=0, t=1, or on the <DEL> step, and almost never on digit inputs.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=a (+5.93), phase=2 & out_tok=c (+4.21), phase=2 & out_tok=v (+3.29), prev2_tok=3 (+2.77), prev_tok=g (+2.64), in_tok=a (+2.42). Lower it: orig_idx=-1 (-2.78), prev2_tok=- (-2.05), L=4 & recall_idx=-1 (-1.80), n_digits=0 (-1.02).
